cards.explanation: The answer is the prophets' words and the Lord's commands. Peter wants them recalling what was foretold by the holy prophets and commanded by our Lord and Savior through their apostles. That's two things in one reminder, friends. Peter packs a lot into one verse, and it's all right there in 2 Peter 3:2.

The answer is True. Peter says the scoffers will ask, “Where is the promise of His coming?” I think it sounds like someone staring at the oven and asking “Is it done yet?” every thirty seconds. Peter says scoffers like that will come in the last days, and he wants believers ready for them.

The answer is continues. The scoffers say, “…everything continues as it has from the beginning of creation.” They say it right after asking where the promise of His coming is. Peter doesn't go along with them, friends, and he's about to say why.

The answer is in the flood. Peter says the world of that time perished in the flood. He ties it to water: the earth was formed out of water and by water, and the world of that time perished through that same water. Peter says the scoffers deliberately overlook this when they say everything continues as it has from the beginning of creation (2 Peter 3:4-6).

The answer is fire. Peter says the present heavens and earth are reserved for fire by that same word. The world of that time perished in the flood, but this present one is being kept for fire. Peter says it's being kept for the day of judgment and destruction of ungodly men (2 Peter 3:7).

The answer is that a day is like a thousand years to Him. Peter says, “With the Lord a day is like a thousand years…” He wants believers, all of us, to keep hold of that and not let it escape their notice. It's the Lord's view of time, and it's different from ours (2 Peter 3:8).

The answer is True. Peter says it both ways: “…a day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years are like a day.” The comparison runs in both directions, friends. Time just doesn't work for the Lord the way it works for us (2 Peter 3:8).

The answer is patient. Peter says the Lord is not slow in keeping His promise as some understand slowness, but is patient with you. So what looks like slowness is patience, friends. That's Peter's own word for it in 2 Peter 3:9.

The answer is everyone to come to repentance. Peter says the Lord is not wanting anyone to perish but everyone to come to repentance. Nobody is left out of that "everyone." That's what the Lord's patience is aimed at (2 Peter 3:9).
The answer is a thief. Peter says the Day of the Lord will come like a thief. He doesn't tell us the day or the hour here, friends. The picture is that it arrives without a warning (2 Peter 3:10).

The answer is False. Peter says the earth and its works will be laid bare. Nothing stays hidden. He says it right after the heavens disappear with a roar and the elements are destroyed by fire (2 Peter 3:10).

The answer is holy and godly in how they live. Peter says, “You ought to conduct yourselves in holiness and godliness…” He's talking about how they live, friends, not just what they believe. The question comes first, then the answer, both in 2 Peter 3:11.

The answer is a new heaven and a new earth. Peter says, “But in keeping with God’s promise, we are looking forward to a new heaven and a new earth…” After all the fire talk, this is the good part, friends. He says it's in keeping with God's promise (2 Peter 3:13).

The answer is righteousness. Peter says the new heaven and new earth are a place “…where righteousness dwells.” It's a place where right living has a home. That's the world believers are looking forward to (2 Peter 3:13).

The answer is spotless and blameless. Peter says to make every effort to be found at peace, and then adds “…spotless and blameless in His sight.” That's how he wants them found while they wait. He says it to believers he calls beloved (2 Peter 3:14).

The answer is salvation. Peter says, “Consider also that our Lord’s patience brings salvation…” The patience he talked about earlier isn't just waiting around, friends. It brings salvation (2 Peter 3:15).

The answer is Paul. Peter says that Paul, whom he calls our beloved brother, also wrote to them with the wisdom God gave him. Peter says Paul wrote about the same matters. He tells them in 2 Peter 3:15.

The answer is True. Peter says, “Some parts of his letters are hard to understand…” He says that about Paul's letters, friends. Peter says ignorant and unstable people distort those parts (2 Peter 3:16).

The answer is to be on their guard. Peter says, “…be on your guard so that you will not be carried away by the error of the lawless…” He says it because they already know these things. Knowing the truth and guarding it go together (2 Peter 3:17).

The answer is their secure standing. Peter says to be on guard so that you will not be carried away by the error of the lawless “…and fall from your secure standing.” The believers have a secure standing, friends, and Peter wants them to keep it. He says it in 2 Peter 3:17.

The answer is grow. Peter says, “But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.” After the warning, this is his final instruction, friends. It's about growing in Jesus Christ, and it's right there in 2 Peter 3:18.
